evals.prompt: Inquiry I-17 revision r2 concluded that a feature was safe to roll out if the error rate stayed below 1%. A monitoring event now reports 1.4% for screen-reader users while the overall rate is 0.4%. Reopen the correct part of the inquiry and preserve provenance.
evals.expected_output: Treats the subgroup guardrail as triggered, creates revision r3, preserves r2, reopens affected framing/measurement/design or decision work, and does not average away the harm.
assertions: Inquiry ID I-17 is preserved and a new revision r3 is created
Revision r2 remains immutable and linked through a Reopen Event
The screen-reader threshold is treated as material despite the aggregate metric
The output identifies the earliest affected artifacts rather than restarting everything automatically
The outcome is routed to learning only after immediate safety/reopening needs are handled

evals.prompt: During synthesis we discover that two supposedly independent surveys used the same respondent panel and copied the same question wording. No world outcome has occurred yet. What changes?
evals.expected_output: Updates dependence, re-evaluates synthesis, and reopens evidence design if support is no longer sufficient without inventing a new external outcome.
assertions: The shared panel and instrument are recorded as common dependencies
The surveys no longer count as two independent corroborations
The Epistemic Profile is revised or the inquiry is reopened at design/synthesis
The output does not fabricate an Outcome Event

evals.prompt: A six-week product experiment met its success threshold, but the decision claimed a one-year reduction in teacher workload. No long-term data have been collected and the monitoring window has expired.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the unsupported temporal bridge and missing monitoring as a reopen condition, distinguishes short-term evidence from the durable claim, and creates a new revision or marks insufficient evidence.
assertions: The six-week result is preserved as evidence within its validity horizon
The one-year workload claim is not validated
A temporal Bridge Claim and its missing evidence are explicit
Expired or absent monitoring is treated as an outcome state rather than success by default

evals.prompt: An audit finds a missing stakeholder but confirms that the existing statistical analysis and telemetry are valid. The missing group may experience a different access mechanism. Reopen proportionately.
evals.expected_output: Reopens framing and affected evidence/product design while preserving validated statistical/telemetry artifacts unless the new frame changes their applicability.
assertions: The new stakeholder and mechanism create a framing revision
The output does not discard validated analysis merely because something reopened
The applicability of prior analysis to the new group is reassessed through scale/basis/construct context
New research or experiment work is scoped to the material gap
